summary: This note is a biographical entry on Edward Winslow (1595-1655), a Separatist who sailed on the Mayflower in 1620 and became a senior leader of Plymouth Colony. It covers his signing of the Mayflower Compact, his governmental roles in the colony, his writings including Mourt's Relation, and his death of fever on a British naval expedition in the Caribbean in 1655.
one_line: Biography of Edward Winslow, Mayflower passenger, Plymouth Colony leader, pamphleteer and co-author of Mourt's Relation, who died in 1655.
key_facts: Edward Winslow was born on 18 October 1595 and died on 8 May 1655.
Edward Winslow was a Separatist who traveled on the Mayflower in 1620.
Edward Winslow and his brother, Gilbert Winslow, both signed the Mayflower Compact.
In Plymouth, Edward Winslow served as assistant governor and three times as governor of the colony.
Edward Winslow also served as the colony's agent in London.
In early 1621, Edward Winslow was one of several key leaders on whom Governor Bradford depended after the death of John Carver.
Edward Winslow authored several important pamphlets, including Good Newes from New England.
Edward Winslow co-wrote Mourt's Relation with William Bradford.
Mourt's Relation ends with an account of the First Thanksgiving and the abundance of the New World.
In 1655, Edward Winslow died of fever while on a British naval expedition in the Caribbean against the Spanish.
Edward Winslow is the only Plymouth colonist with an extant portrait.
The portrait of Edward Winslow can be seen at Pilgrim Hall, Plymouth, Massachusetts.
